steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 57.10 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the flat side on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the RIGHT of the blade. Mitre 21.1° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 45.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, left of the blade, is a tapered piece: 2.70 in along the point, down to 0.50 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the flat side. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).
Saw settings, held as the piece lies in the panel:
10 ends: mitre 30.0°, bevel 45.0° -- the 45° wall of the long edge
10 ends: mitre 60.0°, bevel 0.0° -- meets its mirror on the centre line
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
fitting: The first piece meets the 45° slope with its bark: it touches along one line, and leaves a wedge-shaped gap above it -- caulk it or pack it.
Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
